 Memorial services, celebration of life was held Friday for Dolores Huerta
 Prev 
 Next 
 Tributes began Monday at the California State Capitol in Sacramento. Now, Bakersfield is preparing to honor Huerta's life and legacy with two days of public memorial events. 
 By: 
 23ABC News Staff
 Posted 
 and last updated 
 Share Copy link Facebook Nextdoor X Threads Reddit LinkedIn Email WhatsApp Messenger Print 
 Add KERO as a Google Preferred Source 
 Members of the community paid their respects at a set of community events held for American labor leader and feminist activist Dolores Huerta.
 Huerta died in late October at the age of 96.
 MEMORIAL AND CELEBRATION OF LIFE
 A celebration of life was held at the Dignity Health Convention Center. Watch live in the player below: 
 An interfaith memorial service was held Friday morning.
 Watch the full memorial service in the player below: 
 FULL: Memorial service held for Dolores Huerta 
 8:00 a.m.: Opening blessing by Aztec dancers
 10:00 a.m. – 12:00 p.m.: Interfaith Memorial Service
 12:00 p.m. – 2:00 p.m.: Afternoon break
 2:00 p.m. – 6:00 p.m.: Celebration of Life, tributes, and performances
 Speakers for the event include:
 Eva Longoria 
 CA Governor-elect Becerra  
 Rob Bonta, CA Attorney General  
 Hilda Solis, Congresswoman-elect, 38th Congressional District 
 Teresa Romero (UFW President)  
 David Huerta (SEIU-USWW President) 
 Yvonne Wheeler, LA Fed of Labor  
 Arnulfo De la Cruz (SEIU CA President) 
 Kathy Spillar (President & CEO, Feminist Majority Foundation) 
 Pete Escovedo and Sheila E. 
 Kerry Kennedy  
 Cristela Alonzo 
 Richard Montoya
 Both events were free and open to the public, and no tickets are required.
 ROSARY AND COMMUNITY VIGIL
 A vigil to honor Dolores Huerta was held Thursday evening in Bakersfield, California. 
 Community members joined the service and paid their respects for Huerta.
 Watch that vigil service in the player below: 
 Vigil, memorial services held for American labor leader Dolores Huerta 
 WHO WAS DOLORES HUERTA?
 Her work began in the 1960s in Delano, where she organized farm workers and co-founded the United Farm Workers.
 Timeline: Pivotal moments in Dolores Huerta's life 
 Earlier in 2026, Huerta spoke out about the alleged abuse she experienced while working with Cesar Chavez.
 "I felt that my coming out and saying would’ve hurt the movement, and that’s the only reason I can say," Huerta said in an interview with Latino USA's Maria Hinojosa.
 Hear more from Dolores Huerta in the player below: 
 Dolores Huerta speaks out for the first time on alleged sexual abuse by civil rights leader Cesar Chavez 
 RELATED: Dolores Huerta speaks out for the first time on alleged sexual abuse by civil rights leader Cesar Chavez 
 Huerta went on to say she found strength to speak out following a New York Times article detailing the accounts of other survivors.
 "Their courage has given me the courage also to come out," Huerta added.
 Dolores Huerta: "I have kept this secret long enough. My silence ends here" 
 Learn more about Huerta and her impacts here.
